analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md was changed. The patch at hunk @@ -163,7 +163,14 @@ adds five bullets under 'Unreleased — cache reliability'. The bullets describe cache-attempt byte bounding, preload and tokenizer capacity, cache-planning accounting and concurrency, and a media-request plan metric change. No code, config, auth, attestation, encryption or billing source was supplied, so the described behavior could not be checked against an implementation.

Security-relevant claims in the text, which an integration pass should compare with the code if it is available:
- The cache-attempt bookkeeping change claims it preserves receipt and dispatch ownership checks. It also reclaims late-receipt grace records under byte pressure, up to 64 completed attempts and never live ones.
- Cache-planning concurrency reserves health/control headroom and keeps the original deadline, cancellation and fail-cold behavior.
- Media requests are now counted as 'ineligible' in the plan metrics, with no routing or billing effect.
- Tokenizer preload and fallback are said to fail closed on protocol loss.
- Provider-bound field stripping (user, metadata, safety_identifier, prompt_cache_key) is unchanged context. Related threat entries are T-003, T-041 and A-001.

No change to TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011 authorization, attestation or encryption semantics is stated. Not examined: the Go/Rust/Swift implementations. Documentation-only change, so no findings.
